definitions.explanation: The feeling of being moved or impressed by something excellent or praiseworthy.

examples.japanese: {感心|かんしん}な{子|こ}ですね。
{彼|かれ}の{努力|どりょく}に{感心|かんしん}した。
examples.english: I was impressed by his effort.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{若|わか}いのにとても{礼儀|れいぎ}{正|ただ}しくて、{皆|みな}{感心|かんしん}していた。
examples.english: She was so polite despite being young that everyone was impressed.

notes:
{感心|かんしん} expresses admiration or being impressed. It can function as a noun, suru-verb, or na-adjective.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {感心|かんしん}する (to be impressed)
- {感心|かんしん}な〜 (admirable ~)
- 〜に{感心|かんしん}する (to be impressed by ~)

NEGATIVE USAGE:
- あまり{感心|かんしん}しない/できない: expresses disapproval or not being impressed
- This is a indirect way to criticize something

DISTINCTION:
- {感心|かんしん} vs. {関心|かんしん}: Different kanji!
  - {感心|かんしん}: admiration ({感|かん} = feeling)
  - {関心|かんしん}: interest ({関|かん} = relation)

REGISTER: Neutral to slightly formal
